label: prop:coxeter-parabolic-transversal
title: Parabolic transversals and the Hecke presentation laws at every rank
html:
Proposition. Parabolic transversals and the Hecke presentation laws at every rank

Let (W, S) be a Coxeter system and s_i, s_j a generator pair with m_{ij} = 3 (respectively m_{ij} = 2), and suppose the single word s_i s_j s_i (respectively s_i s_j) is reduced. Then:

  1. the standard parabolic subgroup W_{\{i,j\}} consists of exactly the six elements e, s_i, s_j, s_j s_i, s_i s_j, s_i s_j s_i (respectively the four elements e, s_i, s_j, s_i s_j);
  2. every left coset of W_{\{i,j\}} has a unique minimal-length representative, and the factorization W \;\cong\; C \times W_{\{i,j\}} (minimal representatives times cell) is a bijection with additive lengths, \ell(u \cdot x) = \ell(u) + \ell(x);
  3. on the length-rule module W \to R over any commutative ring, the right-multiplication actions of s_i and s_j satisfy the braid relation (respectively far commutation).

The length additivity is the Bourbaki lifting lemma, obtained unconditionally from the strong exchange property; the coset datum localises each presentation law to a finite cell check. The single reducedness hypothesis per pair is the faithfulness of the dihedral cell — a theorem of Coxeter theory via the geometric representation, which is verified outright for the type-A_3 system by the permutation representation on four letters, so at that rung the braid and far-commutation laws hold with no hypothesis at all. Together with the quadratic relation, which holds outright at every rank, all three defining relation kinds of the Hecke algebra H_n(q) acting on its normal-form basis flow from the Coxeter-system data.
